application_guidance.input_pattern: A deterministic exact first-order optimization claim on a Hadamard manifold with strictly negative upper sectional curvature and the matching radius/condition-number relation.
read_original_when: Changing the Oracle, Algorithm randomness, output convention, metric, or parameter regime.
Using the resisting-oracle construction or interpolation as a reusable Proof component.
Needing independent verification of the full literature Proof.
sensitive_conditions: The quantifier is for every deterministic Algorithm, then there exists f; randomized Algorithms are outside the statement.
Global strong geodesic convexity and local smoothness have different domains.
xref and the ball radius specify prior minimizer localization; x* lies in the smaller ball B(xref,3r/4).
Retain both curvature-ratio factors and the coupling kappa=12r sqrt(-K_lo)+9.
The metric is distance to the minimizer, not function suboptimality or gradient norm.

complexity_scope.guarantee: For every deterministic Algorithm there exists a hard function in the specified class.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: The floor expression retains the numerical constant 1000, logarithm, and curvature-ratio dependence explicitly. Use this expression rather than removing the curvature factor through asymptotic notation.
complexity_scope.oracle: A query at x in M returns (f(x),(x,grad f(x))) exactly; no noise.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Find a point within Riemannian distance r/5 of the unique global minimizer. The source formalizes Algorithms through query/iterate maps; no additional exact-count claim for a separately defined postprocessing-output model is introduced here.
complexity_scope.regime: Strictly negative upper curvature bound, finite lower curvature bound, d>=2, kappa>=1000 sqrt(K_lo/K_up), and kappa=12 r sqrt(-K_lo)+9. Strong geodesic convexity is global; L-smoothness is only required in the known ball.
complexity_scope.resource: Number of exact first-order Oracle queries, each providing value and gradient together. Internal computation is unrestricted in this model and is not separately bounded by this result.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Every deterministic first-order Algorithm in §1.2: arbitrary history-dependent maps and initial point; no span restriction and no bounded-query restriction. This is Oracle Complexity coverage, not the performance of a selected Algorithm.

content.intended_use: A literature lower bound for deterministic exact first-order Algorithms with unrestricted query locations, in the specified coupled radius/condition-number regime.

proofs.locator: §1.1, p.3; Lemma 7, p.6; Appendix F, Theorem 20 and overview, pp.25–26; Appendix G, Theorem 24 and §G.1, pp.31–34; Appendix M.1, p.46
map: §1.1 explains why bare squared-distance functions reveal their center through exact gradients. The source instead perturbs squared-distance functions using compactly supported C-infinity bumps with controlled Hessian.

A1/A2 and Lemma 7, p.6: strict negative upper curvature yields packing at every xref with r_tilde=4/sqrt(-K_up) and c_tilde=d sqrt(-K_up)/8. Packed centers lie in B(xref,3r/4), with pairwise distance at least r/2. The source Proof uses Lemma 6 and the spherical packing result Lemma 27.

Theorem 20, p.25, gives the bounded-query exact value-and-gradient lower bound under A1, curvature in [K_lo,0], r>=max{r_tilde,8/sqrt(-K_lo),4(d+2)/c_tilde}, and technical condition number kappa_0=4r sqrt(-K_lo)+3. Its hard functions are half squared distance plus a C-infinity perturbation satisfying the global value, gradient and Hessian bounds in (20). The p.26 overview identifies bumps controlling both value and gradient, with Lemmas 21–23 supporting the resisting Oracle. Their complete Proofs were not read.

Theorem 24 and §G.1, pp.31–34, remove bounded queries by replacing each hard function outside a larger ball with D(x)=dist(x,xref)^2/2 and using a smooth interpolation. Outside that ball, replies depend only on xref and geometry and require no query to the underlying hard Oracle; inside, at most one underlying query simulates each reply. Figure 1 shows this reduction. §G.1 invokes §G.2 to retain membership in F_{3 kappa_0,r}^{xref}(M); the complete §G.2 Hessian estimates were not checked.

§M.1, p.46, substitutes Lemma 7's packing constants into Theorem 24. It checks the radius prerequisites from kappa>=1000 sqrt(K_lo/K_up), uses kappa=3 kappa_0=12r sqrt(-K_lo)+9, and bounds the explicit query expression below by the floor expression in Theorem 2. This is a map of the source derivation, not a new local transfer Proof.

assumptions: d is an integer with d>=2.
Every sectional curvature of M lies in [K_lo,K_up], where K_lo<=K_up<0 are finite real constants.
xref is any point of M.
r>0 is defined by kappa=12 r sqrt(-K_lo)+9.
The Oracle returns exact function values and Riemannian gradients; the Algorithm is deterministic and may query anywhere in M.
statement.conclusion: A requires at least floor(sqrt(K_up/K_lo) * kappa / (1000 log(10 kappa))) queries to find a point x in M with dist(x,x*)<=r/5, where x* is the minimizer of f. This is the explicit bound in Theorem 2; the source also denotes its scaling by soft-Omega(sqrt(K_up/K_lo) * kappa).
statement.objects_and_definitions: M is a d-dimensional Hadamard manifold: complete, simply connected, with nonpositive sectional curvature. dist is its Riemannian distance; B(a,s) is the closed geodesic ball. F_{kappa,r}^{xref}(M) consists of C-infinity functions f:M->R such that there exist mu>0 and L with L/mu=kappa, Hess f(x)>=mu I for all x in M, ||Hess f(x)||<=L for all x in B(xref,r), and a unique global minimizer x* in B(xref,3r/4). A deterministic first-order Algorithm consists of an initial x0 in M and arbitrary maps A_k:(R x TM)^k->M using the preceding exact transcript (f(x_i),(x_i,grad f(x_i))).
statement.parameter_domains: d>=2; K_lo<=K_up<0; xref in M; kappa>=1000 sqrt(K_lo/K_up); r=(kappa-9)/(12 sqrt(-K_lo)). The radius and condition number are coupled, not independent parameters.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every M, curvature bounds, xref and kappa satisfying these conditions, and for every deterministic first-order Algorithm A in the source model, there exists f in F_{kappa,r}^{xref}(M) on which A requires the stated number of queries. The hard function may depend on A. No randomized-Algorithm guarantee is asserted.
